item.title: Province proclaims Media Literacy Week
item.description:
Province proclaims Media Literacy Week jenniferdhogan Mon, 10/26/2026 - 12:17

During Media Literacy Week, Island students, parents, and educators are encouraged to take part in activities and practices that strengthen digital skills and promote safe, responsible online behaviour.

Taking place October 26-30, Media Literacy Week, is a bilingual national initiative that has raised awareness about the importance of digital media literacy in classrooms, libraries, and communities across Canada for the past 21 years.

"As the digital world continues to evolve, it's becoming increasingly important for children and youth to learn how to navigate AI and their online world in a safe and responsible way. Teaching media literacy can be as simple as encouraging healthy screen habits and helping students think critically about what they see and experience online."

- Minister of Education and Early Years Robin Croucher

The province has taken steps to help young people develop smart screen use behaviours. In fall 2025, Healthy Screen Time Guidelines were introduced in Island schools to help staff make informed decisions about when and how to use technology to support student learning. The guidelines promote student health and well-being through a balanced approach that includes physical activity, social interaction, and hands-on learning.

In June 2026, the province released the Provincial Youth Cyberviolence Prevention Strategy, a cross-government plan to help prevent and protect young people from cyberbullying and other online harm. The provincial government helps put the strategy into action through curriculum, classroom resources, professional learning, and school-based programs.

To learn more or find Media Literacy Week activities and resources, visit MediaSmarts.

item.title: Honouring Mi’kmaq roots through support, healing, and connection
item.description:
Honouring Mi’kmaq roots through support, healing, and connection jenniferdhogan Mon, 10/26/2026 - 09:16

Women have long played an important role in supporting one another, strengthening their communities and creating opportunities for others. For Patsy Gavin, that legacy of women supporting women has shaped more than 40 years of advocacy and volunteer work with the Mi’kmaq community. 

Patsy is president of the Aboriginal Women’s Association of PEI and volunteers with the Sukwisim Healing Lodge and the Mi’kmaq Family Resource Centre. Across these organizations, she works to ensure Indigenous women and children have access to support, opportunities to learn, and connections to their culture and community. 

As a day school survivor, Patsy’s own experiences have shaped her healing journey and the work she does today. Her connection to the Aboriginal Women’s Association began when she was young. Over the years, the organization became a place where she could learn about Mi’kmaq culture, develop new skills, and find support. Today, she helps create those same opportunities for other women. 

“I don’t do this work for myself. I do it for the children, the next generation and the generation after that,” she says. 

Through education, advocacy, and traditional skills such as beadwork and moccasin making, the Aboriginal Women’s Association helps women build confidence, share knowledge, and strengthen their cultural connections. At the Sukwisim Healing Lodge, Patsy supports a Circle of Care approach that recognizes healing takes time and that support is often needed beyond formal treatment.

Patsy credits her mother, Marilyn Sark, and the other women who led before her with teaching her the importance of leadership, perseverance, and community. Their influence continues to guide her as she works with other women to create spaces where people feel heard, supported, and connected.

For Patsy, that work is also about recognizing the strength and resilience of the Mi’kmaq community. 

“We’re still here.” she says

Patsy describes herself as deeply maternal. Although she was unable to have children of her own, she has devoted much of her life to supporting women and children and building a better future for the generations to come. 

That commitment is reflected in her message to those who will carry this work forward. She says, “Remember that you’re only a small part of history, but your choices can affect future generations.” 

Through October, the Government of Prince Edward Island is celebrating Women’s History Month by highlighting women whose leadership, advocacy, and commitment to community are creating opportunities and helping shape a stronger future for generations of Island women.

Groundwork: From Soil to Sustenance

From building healthy soils and managing pests and disease to exploring new crops, production methods, and ways to make a farm more resilient, Groundwork brings together the knowledge and lived experience that help farms thrive.

Join ACORN for two days of practical learning, conversation, and connection with fellow farmers and growers from across Atlantic Canada.

Whether you’re a seasoned farmer, just getting started, exploring more ecological ways to grow, or simply curious about where our food comes from, you're welcome at the table.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
